files_summary.repo_metadata.json: Repository metadata for github/gitignore including fields such as id, node_id, name, full_name, private flag, owner (login, id, type), html_url, description, timestamps (created_at, updated_at, pushed_at), clone URLs, size, stargazers_count, watchers_count, language, issue/project/download/wiki/pages/discussions flags, forks_count, open_issues_count, and default_branch.
files_summary.issues_prs.json: Array of recent pull request issues (open PRs) from the gitignore repository. Each entry contains: url, number, title, user (login), state, created_at timestamp, body (excerpt), and a nested pull_request object with its API URL and HTML URL.
files_summary.commits.json: Array of recent commit objects for the repository. Each entry includes: sha (commit hash), author name, date (ISO timestamp), and full commit message (including PR merge messages where applicable).
files_summary.contents.json: Array of root directory entries of the repository. Each entry includes name, type (file or dir), path, size (for files), and download_url (direct raw file URL) where applicable.
files_summary.commands.json:
Array of objects, each representing a command available in the Terminal environment. Each object contains:
- "name": the command name (e.g., "ls", "git").
- "description": a concise description sourced from TLDR pages or command help output.
- "category": logical grouping such as "File Management", "Networking", "System Information", "Compression/Archiving", "Version Control", "Programming", "Container Management", "Process Management", "Security", or "Miscellaneous".
The file includes entries for all commands listed in the environment definition (e.g., dirname, python, traceroute, file, netstat, cut, clear, find, cp, git, ping, curl, basename, tail, sort, history, md5sum, gunzip, which, mv, sha256sum, touch, pwd, gzip, wget, zip, ps, cat, diff, stat, more, env, head, ifconfig, uniq, du, tar, mkdir, nslookup, kubectl, realpath, date, hostname, df, wc, tr, echo, awk, rm, chmod, sed, ls, unzip, whoami, less, grep, cd, helm, tree).
files_summary.toolsets.json:
JSON object describing the Terminal toolset:
- "toolset_name": "Terminal".
- "description": Brief description of the environment providing command execution and security introspection.
- "tools": Array of tool definitions:
  * "run_command": Executes a single CLI command in the `/workspace/dumps/workspace` directory, supporting all standard shell operators. Parameters: `command` (string, required).
  * "show_security_rules": Returns the allowed commands and operations in this environment. No parameters.
- "allowed_shell_operators": true (indicates that shell operators like &&, ||, |, >, etc., are permitted).
- "default_directory": "/workspace/dumps/workspace".
files_summary.security_rules.json:
JSON object defining security configuration for the Terminal service:
- "allow_shell_operators": true.
- "allowed_commands": List of all command names extracted from `commands.json` (e.g., "dirname", "python", "traceroute", … "tree").
- "disallowed_commands": Empty array (no commands are explicitly blocked).
- "allowed_tools": ["run_command", "show_security_rules"].
files_summary.README.md: Schema, lifecycles and business rules of this benchmark's datastore.

tool_schemas.name: get_repo_metadata
tool_schemas.description: Returns the repository snapshot metadata object, optionally reduced to only the requested top-level fields. If `fields` is provided, we only include fields that exist in the metadata and refuse requests where `fields` is not an array of strings. We also refuse requests that ask for no usable fields (for example, an empty `fields` list), because there would be nothing to return.

fields.description: List of metadata fields to include. If omitted, returns the full metadata object.

tool_schemas.name: list_issues_prs
tool_schemas.description: Returns a list of issues and pull requests from the snapshot, or a single entry when `number` is provided, optionally filtered by `state` and/or opener `user` and optionally reduced to selected fields. We refuse requests with an invalid `state`, a non-integer `number`/`limit`, a `limit` that is not positive, or a `fields` value that is not an array of strings. When `number` is provided, we refuse the request if that issue/PR number does not exist in the snapshot.

user.description: Filter by the login of the user who opened the issue/PR.

number.description: Retrieve a specific issue/PR by its number.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20).

fields.description: List of fields to include for each entry.

tool_schemas.name: list_commits
tool_schemas.description: Returns a list of commits from the snapshot, or a single commit when `sha` is provided, optionally filtered by `author` and/or a time window and optionally reduced to selected fields. We refuse requests where `since`/`until` are not valid ISO date-time strings, where `since` is after `until`, where `limit` is not a positive integer, or where `fields` is not an array of strings. When `sha` is provided, we refuse the request if that commit SHA is not present in the snapshot.

since.description: Only include commits after this ISO timestamp.

until.description: Only include commits before this ISO timestamp.

sha.description: Retrieve a specific commit by its SHA.

limit.description: Maximum number of commits to return (default 20).

fields.description: List of fields to include for each commit.

tool_schemas.name: list_root_contents
tool_schemas.description: Returns entries from the repository root snapshot, optionally filtered by `entry_type` and/or `path_prefix` and optionally reduced to selected fields. We refuse requests with an `entry_type` other than `file` or `dir`, a `limit` that is not a positive integer, or a `fields` value that is not an array of strings. We also refuse requests where `path_prefix` is not a string.

entry_type.description: Filter entries by type (file or dir).

path_prefix.description: Only include entries whose path starts with this prefix.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 20).

fields.description: List of fields to include for each entry.

tool_schemas.name: list_commands
tool_schemas.description: Returns a list of available terminal commands from the snapshot, optionally filtered by `category`, exact `name`, or `name_prefix`, and optionally reduced to the selected fields. We refuse requests that include any parameters other than the documented ones, a `limit` that is not a positive integer, or a `fields` list containing anything other than `name`, `description`, or `category`. If both `name` and `name_prefix` are provided, we refuse the request because those filters conflict.

name.description: Filter commands by exact command name.

name_prefix.description: Only include commands whose name starts with this prefix.

limit.description: Maximum number of commands to return (default 20).

fields.description: List of fields to include for each command.

tool_schemas.name: get_command
tool_schemas.description: Returns the command definition that matches the provided command `name`. We refuse requests missing `name` or where `name` is not a string. We also refuse the request if no command with that exact name exists in the snapshot.

name.description: The name of the command to retrieve.

tool_schemas.name: list_commands_by_category
tool_schemas.description: Returns all commands whose category matches the provided `category`. We refuse requests missing `category` or where `category` is not a string. We also refuse the request if the category does not exist in the snapshot (meaning it would match no commands).

category.description: The category to filter commands by (e.g., "File Management", "Networking").

tool_schemas.name: get_toolset
tool_schemas.description: Returns one toolset definition from the snapshot (name, description, tools, allowed shell operators, default directory), optionally reduced to only the requested fields. We refuse requests that include any parameters other than the documented ones, a `fields` list containing unknown field names, or a `fields` value that is not an array. If `toolset_name` is provided, we refuse the request when that toolset does not exist in the snapshot.

toolset_name.description: Retrieve a specific toolset by its toolset_name.

fields.description: List of fields to include. If omitted, returns the full toolset object.

tool_schemas.name: get_security_rules
tool_schemas.description: Returns the terminal security rules snapshot, optionally reduced to only the requested fields. We refuse requests that include any parameters other than the documented ones, a `fields` list containing unknown field names, or a `fields` value that is not an array. We also refuse requests that ask for no usable fields (for example, an empty `fields` list), because there would be nothing to return.

fields.description: List of fields to include. If omitted, returns the full security rules object.

tool_schemas.name: get_readme
tool_schemas.description: Returns the repository README contents either as the raw source (`raw`) or as plain text (`text`). We refuse requests that include any parameters other than the documented ones or a `format` other than `raw` or `text`. We also refuse the request if the README content is not available in the snapshot.

format.description: Return format for the README contents.

metadata.name: Harborview Repo Navigator
metadata.description: Provides a read-only, queryable snapshot of repository metadata, commits, issues/PRs, contents, command catalogs, toolsets, and security rules for downstream browsing and filtering.
